nodes.summary: The pair of statistics `(X, Y)` is exchangeable under `μ`: the joint law is unchanged by swapping the two coordinates. This is an additional calibration assumption for a two-group haplotype test, stronger than the ordinary neutral null. Defined as `IdentDistrib` of the two orderings, so the measurability of the joint laws is part of the hypothesis rather than restored separately in each theorem.
nodes.title: Exchangeable pair of statistics

nodes.summary: Applying the same measurable function to both statistics preserves exchangeability.
nodes.title: Exchangeability is preserved by a common measurable map

nodes.summary: The difference of an exchangeable pair has a symmetric law.
nodes.title: Difference of an exchangeable pair has a symmetric law

nodes.summary: A two-sided rejection region splits into two tails of equal probability.
nodes.title: Two-sided rejection region splits into equal tails

nodes.summary: For positive statistics, the log ratio — the XP-EHH form — has equal tails.
nodes.title: Equal tails of the log ratio of an exchangeable pair

nodes.summary: The same statement for the ratio itself, the form used for relative EHH: the probability that the ratio exceeds `c` equals the probability that it falls below `1 / c`.
nodes.title: Equal tails of the ratio of an exchangeable pair

nodes.summary: Equal tails: the upper tail of `X - Y` at `t` has the same probability as the lower tail at `-t`.
nodes.title: Equal tails of the difference of an exchangeable pair

nodes.summary: Under exchangeability, the XP-EHH score has a symmetric law: the two tails of the two-sided test carry the same probability.
nodes.title: Symmetry of the XP-EHH law under exchangeability

nodes.summary: XP-EHH computed from two star-genealogy sweep models with the same recombination rate is the log ratio of the two ages, with the opposite sign to `ihs`.
nodes.title: XP-EHH in star-genealogy sweep models

nodes.summary: The cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity score (Sabeti et al. 2007): the log ratio of the integrated haplotype homozygosities of the same core region in two populations. Both arguments must be positive for the score to be meaningful. Outside that domain `Real.log` is totalized by Mathlib, not by the stated junk value: `Real.log 0 = 0` and `Real.log (-x) = Real.log x`, so for example…
nodes.title: Cross-population extended haplotype homozygosity (XP-EHH)

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
